subtopics.title: The Vocabulary of the Circle and the Chord Theorems

questions.question: The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord:
options: Passes through the point of contact of a tangent

questions.question: A chord of length 24 lies in a circle of radius 13. Its distance from the centre is:
In the chord-distance triangle, the side you must use is:
options: Half the chord — the perpendicular from the centre bisects it

questions.question: The perpendicular bisector of any chord always:
options: Is parallel to the tangent at one endpoint
Has the same length as the radius
Cuts the circle into equal segments
Passes through the centre of the circle

subtopics.title: The Angle at the Centre Is Double the Angle at the Circumference

questions.question: If the angle at the centre on an arc is 120°, every circumference angle on that arc is:
A reflex centre angle of 200° means the circumference angle on that same (major) arc is:
The proof of the centre theorem draws a line from the circumference point through the centre and leans on:
options: Isosceles triangles from radii plus the exterior angle theorem

questions.question: Every angle at the circumference standing on a diameter equals:
Angles subtended by the same chord, from the same side of it, are:
Chord AB subtends 47° at C. D lies on the same arc as C. Angle ADB is:
The one-line proof of the same-segment theorem says both angles equal:
options: The angle between the chord and the tangent
Half the same central angle on that arc
The angle sum of the triangle
Half the reflex angle at the centre

questions.question: Two angles on the same chord but on opposite sides of it are:
options: Not equal — they lie in different segments

subtopics.title: Riders — Reading the Diagram and Writing Reasons

questions.question: In circle geometry marking, a true statement without its reason earns:
options: Nothing — every line needs claim plus reason

questions.question: O is the centre and angle AOB = 80° on the minor arc. For C on the major arc, angle ACB is:
options: 40° — angle at centre is twice angle at circumference

questions.question: In the same rider, triangle AOB has apex angle 80°, so each base angle is:
options: 50° — radii make it isosceles, then the angle sum

questions.question: The first move when reading any rider diagram is to:
options: Write the final answer and work backwards
Darken every radius — two radii make an isosceles triangle

questions.question: Folding a paper circle so a chord's endpoints meet produces a crease that:
options: Bisects the chord at right angles and passes through the centre
Touches the circle at one point

questions.question: For a chord of 24 in a circle of radius 13, the fold-line (distance to centre) is:
Folding along two different chords finds the centre because:
options: Each crease is a perpendicular bisector, and all of them pass through the centre
The creases are both diameters of the folded shape
Paper always folds through the centre

subtopics.title: The Whole Stadium Sees the Same Game

questions.question: Every seat on the same arc, watching the same goal-chord, sees it at:
options: A smaller angle the further along the arc you sit
Exactly the same angle — angles in the same segment

questions.question: The centre sees the goal at 120°. A seat on the far arc sees it at:
If the goal-chord is a full diameter, every seat on the curve sees it at:
options: 90° — half of the straight 180° at the centre

questions.question: Before halving a centre angle, you must first:
options: Shade the arc that both angles actually stand on
Draw the tangent at one endpoint

subtopics.title: Solving a Rider Like a Case File

questions.question: The detective's opening move on any rider is:
options: Darken the radii and hunt for a diameter

questions.question: Centre angle 80° at the apex of the radii triangle: the two base angles are:
Each line of a rider solution should:
options: Lean on an earlier certainty and carry its own reason
Stand completely independent of the others

questions.question: An answer with correct values but no reasons is:
options: Awarded nothing for the unreasoned claims — like a case with no evidence
